h: Chocolate, sharks and science in Brum
p: A good tip for inflatable parks is to pace yourself. The temptation is to race the obstacle course flat out from the off, but those climbs and slides add up, and by the halfway mark plenty of grown-ups are wheezing. Take the first few runs at a steady pace, find your favourite bits, then go all out at the end. Arrive with enough time to sort shoes, socks and coats, and agree a meeting point in case anyone gets separated in the excitement.

Birmingham is brilliant for a second activity. Thinktank, the science museum at Millennium Point, has hands-on galleries, a planetarium and loads of old machines and engines, perfect for curious kids. Over at Brindleyplace, the National SEA LIFE Centre has sharks, turtles and a walk-through ocean tunnel, so you can swap one indoor adventure for another if the weather's grim.

Chocolate lovers should know that Cadbury World is in Bournville, on the south side of the city, with exhibits on how chocolate is made and, crucially, a few freebies along the way. The Library of Birmingham in Centenary Square has rooftop garden terraces with great views over the city, and it's free to visit. Birmingham New Street has trains from all over the country, and the tram runs through the centre if you'd rather not drive between stops. For a bit of fresh air, the Lickey Hills on the south-western edge of the city have woodland trails and viewpoints over the Worcestershire countryside, a lovely way to wind down after a busy indoor session.
